answer: Verifiable Effort Ledger. Each agent identity must accumulate a ledger of solved, independently checked micro-tasks (e.g., labeling rare juniper disease images) before gaining write access. The rule: one identity, one ledger, no transfer. An attacker must spend real compute and human review hours per identity, and each yarrow-species classification task is audited by two random peers. Forgery costs the full task volume plus audit rejection, and jade-marked validator signatures bind results, so mass registration multiplies work, not just money.
